author: P. V. Crane
title: Pearl Cecil named to U.S. roster for FIFA U20 Women's World Cup
text:
Pearl Cecil named to U.S. roster for FIFA U20 Women’s World Cup
P. V. Crane
Sophomore defender Pearl Cecil was named to the United States roster for the FIFA Under-20 Women’s World Cup by head coach Vicky Jepsen, according to a U.S. Soccer announcement on Aug. 19. The tournament will be hosted by Poland and is scheduled to run from September 5 through September 27.
The United States team will begin group play against Italy on Sunday, September 6 at Stadion Miejski LKS Lodz in Lodz, with kickoff set for noon Eastern Time (6 p.m. local), broadcast on FOX Soccer Plus. The second match will be against Japan, a finalist in the previous FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup, on Wednesday, September 9 at the same venue and time, airing on FS2. The final group stage match is set for Saturday, September 12 against New Zealand at Arena Sosnowiec in Sosnowiec at 9 a.m. Eastern Time (3 p.m. local) and will be shown on FS1. All matches of the tournament are scheduled to be broadcast in English across FOX networks.
“This group wears the crest with honor, and we’re excited to see what they can accomplish together,” Jepson said. “They all have tremendous pride in earning this opportunity to represent their country on the world’s biggest stage for their age group. We really want to thank the NWSL clubs and the colleges for their collaboration in releasing their players for this tournament, as it will be a once-in-a-lifetime chance for many of them and we know it will be an invaluable growth experience for these young women on their soccer journeys.”
Four players from this year’s Under-20 Women’s World Cup roster previously played in last year’s FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup held in Morocco: goalkeeper Evan O’Steen, defender Pearl Cecil, midfielder Nyanya Touray, and forward Micayla Johnson each represented the United States at that event—one player from each positional line.
Cecil played every minute of all four games during last year’s Under-17 tournament and captained her team three times.
